subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should this umbrella remain open until maintainers accept or reject the guarded cron base-session cleanup and the default-off recurring cadence guardrail, or should the remaining slices be split or rejected now?
rationale: The source-backed retention bug is real, but the full request spans compatibility-sensitive session-state cleanup and a new operator-facing scheduling policy that automation should not decide unilaterally.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Until Linked PRs Settle
options.body: Track the combined user problem here while reviewing the retention and cadence PRs, then split only verified leftovers after those decisions land.

options.title: Split Remaining Work Now
options.body: Create narrower canonical issues for retention cleanup, cadence guardrails, context warnings, and sessions cleanup before narrowing this issue.

options.title: Reject Core Cadence Policy
options.body: Keep the retention bug path open but explicitly close or narrow the cadence-guardrail slice if core should not own that policy.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Until Linked PRs Settle
recommendation.body: Track the combined user problem here while reviewing the retention and cadence PRs, then split only verified leftovers after those decisions land.

likelyOwner.reason: The active cron.minInterval PR is the clearest remaining product/config decision in this umbrella, while the retention slice already has a guarded candidate fix.
